holidays.name: National Day of the Horse
holidays.description: A day to salute horses and their long partnership with humans, from farm work to transportation to companionship. Stables and riding clubs celebrate with extra carrots, grooming sessions, and trail rides.
holidays.origin: The U.S. Congress designated December 13 as National Day of the Horse in 2004 through a resolution recognizing the horse's contributions to American history and culture.
holidays.funFact: Horses can sleep both standing up and lying down, thanks to a special stay apparatus in their legs that lets them lock their joints and doze while upright.

holidays.name: National Cocoa Day
holidays.description: A day to wrap your hands around a steaming mug of hot chocolate. Marshmallows, whipped cream, peppermint sticks, and a dash of cinnamon are all encouraged.
holidays.origin: National Cocoa Day is an unofficial food holiday that is observed in December, when cold weather makes hot cocoa especially popular. It is widely celebrated on social media and in cafes.
holidays.funFact: The Aztecs and Maya drank chocolate as a bitter, frothy, spiced beverage long before anyone thought to add sugar to it.

holidays.name: National Ice Cream Day (Ice Cream and Violins Day)
holidays.description: A quirky observance pairing frozen treats with string music. The idea is to enjoy ice cream while listening to violins, or at least to imagine you are in a fancy ice cream parlor with a tiny orchestra.
holidays.origin: Ice Cream and Violins Day is a whimsical unofficial observance listed in many holiday calendars for December 13. Its exact origin is unclear, which adds to its charm.
holidays.funFact: Ice cream sold in winter is more common than people think, and surveys regularly show that many people eat it all year round regardless of the temperature outside.

holidays.name: Santa Lucia Day
holidays.description: A festival of light celebrated especially in Sweden and other Nordic countries. Children dress in white robes with red sashes, and the girl chosen as Lucia wears a crown of candles while the household enjoys saffron buns and ginger biscuits.
holidays.origin: It honors Saint Lucy of Syracuse, a Christian martyr from the 4th century. Her feast day fell near the winter solstice in the old Julian calendar, so it became a symbol of light in the darkest time of the year.
holidays.funFact: Lussekatter, the traditional saffron buns of Santa Lucia Day, are shaped in curled S-forms and often topped with raisins, and Sweden even holds a national Lucia pageant to choose a new Lucia each year.

holidays.name: National Day of the Horse Cousin: Wear Your Plaid Day
holidays.description: A cozy and slightly absurd fashion observance on which people are encouraged to wear plaid, from flannel shirts to tartan scarves, and proudly clash patterns with their friends.
holidays.origin: This is an informal social media era observance that grew out of winter flannel season and holiday plaid traditions, with no single official founder.
holidays.funFact: Plaid is the American name for what Scots call tartan, and in Scotland the word plaid originally meant a blanket-like garment rather than the pattern itself.
